title: Tutorials: the Redlining track
goal:
The track for the app's primary real job: measuring a real screen and handing somebody a spec. Measure a gap, measure a size, check alignment, collect the measurements, export the spec.

The guides in this track: Measure a gap; Measure something's size; Let it snap, or drag it free; The Measurements panel; Export a spec list.
notes:
One of the seven track tasks. Depends on the framework task and on the Help menu IA task.

What this track is for: This is the user's main use of the app, so it is the track most worth being excellent. Source of truth is docs/design/next-measure.md. The measure tool has modes behind a flyout on its button (ToolModeButton, and the tool button at EditorView.swift:1793) and its snapping and roles live behind feature flags in FeatureCatalog - a guide must not point at a control a flag has switched off. Say in the audit how a guide behaves when the feature it teaches is flagged off: skipped, or shown as unavailable.

Write the guides as DATA in the catalogue. If a guide in this track cannot be expressed without new framework machinery, that is a finding: file it against the framework rather than special casing it here, and say so in the audit.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for every tutorials task (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12):

The user's words: "I would like a help > tutorials > * set of guides which walks you through basics of various features. Maybe a nice getting started tutorial, maybe a 'building components' walkthrough, etc. ... And maybe a first run experience which lets you get an intro to the app, or just gogogo. Use the design clickthroughs as inspiration, where you have pointers and can point to various parts of the application. Build a nice framework for defining these walkthroughs so that we can extend it over time. I'd like the tutorials system to be well organized and not just a long list of things."

The agreed shape (settled in the intake conversation, 2026-09-12):
- TRACKS, not a flat list. Help > Tutorials holds "Take the Tour" plus one SUBMENU per track, and a Tutorials window is the hub. The tracks are: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video.
- A guide is DATA, not code: a Codable value in PhotonzCore describing steps. Adding a guide means adding data to the catalogue, and the menu, the window and the progress list all pick it up with no UI edited. That is the whole point of the framework and the thing that makes it extensible.
- Steps POINT AT REAL UI, clickthrough-style: a callout with a pointer aimed at a named control, not a page of prose.
- Design doc: docs/design/tutorials.md is the source of truth for the framework and the track list, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.

THE TRAP that will waste a runner's day if it is not read first: the app already has a registry of named UI targets, the playtest harness (playtestControl / playtestField / steady names, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift). It looks like exactly the right thing to reuse and it is NOT USABLE here: it is compiled out of the shipping build (Scripts/build-app.sh defines PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST for the dev and probe variants only, see docs/design/playtest-harness.md, "Who can run it"), and PanelTarget.swift:141 onwards is the no-op stub release actually gets. Tutorials ship to users, so the anchor registry has to be its own thing that is compiled IN for release. Model it on the playtest one - especially the STEADY NAME idea at PanelTarget.swift:126-138, a name taken off the model rather than off the copy, so rewording a label cannot break a guide - but do not depend on it.

Existing surfaces a tutorial entry point must fit with rather than duplicate:
- The Welcome window (Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift), first-run permissions setup, re-reachable from the menu-bar menu as "Welcome & Permissions...". It already owns first launch.
- The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615): open a file, capture a rectangle, paste an image, blank canvas.
- There is NO Help menu in the app today: EditorCommands.swift declares Capture, Image, Video, Layer and the standard groups, and macOS supplies the default Help menu. Help > Tutorials has to be created.

Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release unless the task says otherwise (CLAUDE.md), and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Every guide in the track exists in the catalogue as data and appears under its track in the Help menu and the Tutorials window with no UI edited
Every guide runs start to finish in the real app, pointing at real controls, each one captured step by step in the audit
Every guide is short: a person can finish one in the time the entry claims, and the claim is measured rather than guessed
Every step points at something a person can actually see at that moment: nothing points at a control that is scrolled out of view, disabled or behind a closed panel without opening it first
A guide that needs something on the canvas brings its own sample document rather than depending on what the person has open
Copy obeys the repo rules: no em dashes, nothing about the tooling that built it, plain short human sentences
Every guide is checked with the features it teaches flagged off as well as on, and behaves sensibly either way
Audit under queue/audits/ with each guide captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: adversarial review before building: the mock-ish plan of five guides holds up, but three things it assumes are not true of the app. (1) The modes live behind the Measure button's own flyout and the I key, so a first-timer cannot find Gap at all: the two measuring guides spend their first two steps there on purpose. (2) The tutorial sample is live shapes over a white canvas, and the measure detector reads PIXELS, so Size and Gap would have found nothing: the redlining samples are flattened into the picture first. (3) A guide about a LIST needs a list with something in it: the panel and export guides bring a screen that arrives already measured. Also cut: a role colours step (it needs a third flag to be true) and a panel menu step (the track says keys, not menus).

framework grew four ways rather than being special cased, all declarative: TutorialSample.isFlattened plus pictureLayers (a sample can be a picture), TutorialGuide.requires plus TutorialCatalog.guides(enabled:) (a guide says which features it needs and is left out when they are off), triggers .measureMode and .specListCopied wired where they happen, and TutorialRun.stepWasAlreadyTrue.

the already-true rule came out of a real failure, not a theory: the snapping walk hung for its whole timeout on 'press I until it reads Distance' because the tool was already in Distance, so nothing fired and the only way on was Skip This Step. A waiting step whose STATE already holds now offers a plain Next. Only a state qualifies; an event like editMade never does.
the size guide used to end on its own click, so the guide evaporated the moment you measured, with no closing word. Every guide now ends on a step you press Done on, and a track test pins it.

five walks, all green, each one driving the guide the way a person would: tutorial-measure-a-gap, tutorial-measure-a-size, tutorial-snap-or-free, tutorial-measurements-panel, tutorial-export-a-spec-list. Measured numbers from the runs: the Save button reads 104 x 38, which is exactly its size; the gap between the buttons reads 25 for a real 24 (gap measures whitespace to the probe-side landings); command frees a dragged foot to land exactly where the pointer stopped; shift holds the row while the pointer wanders 60 down; control-command-C put the three line spec list on the clipboard and shift-command-C put the picture and the same list.

flags off was proved two ways: a unit test over the catalogue, and one probe run with the three measure flags written off by hand (defaults write com.dzearing.photonz.probe experiments.next.flags). With them off the Redlining submenu is gone from Help and the shelf is gone from the Tutorials window, with nothing dimmed. A walk for it passed either way, since a walk cannot set flags, so it was deleted rather than left in the sweep as noise, and the gap is filed as a-walk-can-switch-a-feature-off-before-it-runs.

ten guides made the Tutorials window scroll, and four Start buttons that had scrolled away read as saying nothing, which failed tutorial-hub-walk. WindowReadProbe.fullReading now reads the window all the way down, and the check is stronger than before: every guide must have a button that says its own name.

follow-ups filed: a-walk-can-switch-a-feature-off-before-it-runs, a-walk-can-click-a-row-in-the-measurements-panel, running-a-whole-tutorials-track-should-not-leave. The alignment guide the goal's prose mentions is left as a question on the audit rather than filed, since the track's own guide list does not include it.

second adversarial pass, on the built thing, found two real faults and both are fixed. The snapping guide's last step pointed at the Measure Tool settings and pointed at NOTHING: placing a caliper hands the pointer back, and that section is only in the panel while the tool is in hand, so the card fell to the middle of the window. The step moved to before the drawing. Every step of every guide now resolves to a real on-screen rectangle, which the walk logs record step by step.

the time claim is measured rather than guessed now, and for the whole catalogue rather than this track: TutorialLength works a guide's length out from its own words, a beat per step and longer again per waiting step, and a test fails any guide whose claim is more than a minute from that. Today's ten guides read 50s to 111s against claims of 1 and 2 minutes.

acceptance walked one by one: (1) five guides in the catalogue as data, and the Help submenu and the hub window both list them with no menu or window code naming any of them; (2) all five run start to finish in the probe, each with its own walk, and the walk logs carry every step's anchor; (3) claims measured, see above; (4) no step points at anything off screen, proved by the anchor line in each walk log; (5) every guide brings its own sample; (6) copy rules enforced by test; (7) flags off proved by test and by one probe run; (8) audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-tutorials-redlining-track.json with a shot per guide.

Five Redlining guides live as data in the catalogue: Measure a gap, Measure something's size, Let it snap or drag it free, The Measurements panel, Export a spec list. Help > Tutorials > Redlining and the Tutorials window both list them with no code naming any of them. Framework grew four declarative ways: a sample can be a flattened picture (the measure detector reads pixels, and the old sample had none), a guide says which feature flags it needs and is dropped when they are off, two new triggers (measure mode, spec list copied), and a step asking for something already true offers Next instead of stranding you on Skip. Verified in the probe: five walks green plus the whole tutorial and measure sets, every step's anchor resolving to a real rectangle, the Save button reading 104 x 38 exactly, command freeing a dragged foot, shift holding the row, and one copy carrying picture plus spec list. Flags off checked by unit test and by one probe run with the measure flags written off: the shelf vanishes from Help and from the window. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-13-tutorials-redlining-track.json. Three follow-ups filed. Committed 1708d30a and pushed.
